decisive_items: compression of the left common iliac vein by the overlying right common iliac artery
Doppler ultrasonography of the left lower extremity demonstrated extensive deep vein thrombosis
response.rationale: The CT finding of left common iliac vein compression by the right common iliac artery is diagnostic of May-Thurner syndrome, which explains the secondary DVT. Antiphospholipid syndrome is excluded by negative antibody testing.

rejected.why: Antiphospholipid antibodies, lupus anticoagulant, and anti-beta-2-glycoprotein antibodies were all negative, so this diagnosis is not supported.
Deep vein thrombosis is present but is a complication of the underlying iliac vein compression rather than the most likely primary diagnosis.
